answer.rationale: The 18% mandate and the expiring contract are the binding constraints; the line at 94% of committed volume with no buffer makes a full primary-vendor switch the highest delivery-risk option in the window. memory_c2 supports that the low-cost vendor can onboard and invoice reliably, and memory_c4 supports that benchmarking against a credible market quote moves the incumbent on price and terms. Using the low-cost quote as leverage to renegotiate with the incumbent targets the mandate while preserving the integration stability recorded in memory_c1, and memory_c6 suggests a multi-year commitment could unlock additional volume pricing to close any gap to 18%. Switching remains the fallback if the incumbent cannot meet the benchmark; adding a second source and deferral are deferred to next review given the single-decision capacity and the 14-day expiry.
